Swift Plumbing (C-12) has been asked for an earliest confirmed time and has not replied. Escalated P1 as ESC-105.

Landlord informed of the emergency and the booking; ask for any spend above £250 to be approved first

boundaries: The HeatRight visit on 11 Oct was a no-show, so the heating is not fixed and no work has been done.
Emailing the landlord does not mean they approved spend on this job. There is no job-specific landlord decision in their own words.
No quote, invoice or cost exists yet.
No new visit time is booked with Swift Plumbing; it has not confirmed one.

Check the visit log date (11 Oct) against today (10 Oct) and fix the ticket classification (urgent vs emergency)

decision.summary: HeatRight Ltd (C-11) was assigned for 11 Oct 08:00-12:00 after one retry (A1), and the tenant visit was set (A2). The tenant and landlord were emailed (A3, A4). The visit log shows HeatRight did not attend, so the no-show was recorded (A5), the tenant was apologised to (A6), Swift Plumbing (C-12) was asked for an earliest confirmed slot (A7), and the job was escalated P1 (ESC-105).

answers.question: 1. What happened when you assigned the contractor and how did you verify it?
answers.answer: The first assign_contractor call failed with HTTP 500 and was NOT APPLIED (ledger A1, attempt 1; ticket was at stage init). The retry succeeded: read-back shows R-4820 at stage visit with HeatRight Ltd (C-11), window 2026-10-11 08:00-12:00 (A1, attempt 2). set_visit for 2026-10-11 08:00 with tenant access was verified (A2).

answers.question: 2. What do you tell the tenant at each point?
answers.answer: Before the visit: HeatRight is booked for Sunday 11 Oct 8am-12pm, keep the morning free, with gas and 999 safety advice (A3, MSG-101). After the no-show: an apology, the job is treated as an emergency, Swift Plumbing is being arranged, no time will be given until it is confirmed, and safety advice again (A6, MSG-103).

answers.question: 3. After the no-show, what do you do?
answers.answer: Record the missed appointment (A5). Tell the tenant (A6). Ask Swift Plumbing (C-12) to confirm the earliest slot (A7). Escalate P1 to maintenance (A8, ESC-105) because heating is still off for a vulnerable tenant. Book C-12 only after they confirm a time.

Blocked by policy because the standing CRM note is not in the case as a landlord reply. Not recorded. Landlord asked by email to confirm (A4).

conflicts: Ticket urgency is 'urgent', but policy treats no heating for a vulnerable occupant as an emergency. Treated as emergency.
The visit log is dated 11 Oct, after today (10 Oct). The no-show was processed as given, but the date needs checking.
The landlord's standing note allows emergency approval without asking, but it is not a job-specific decision. Not treated as recorded approval.
assumptions: Emergency classification applies because the tenant is flagged vulnerable and has no heating or hot water.
The 08:00-12:00 window on 11 Oct is the system window for HeatRight. HeatRight has not itself confirmed it, but the tenant was told it is booked.
Email is the tenant's preferred channel, as recorded in the CRM.

args.body:
Dear Jonah,

Thank you for reporting that you have no heating or hot water. We are treating this as an emergency because of the cold weather.

We have booked HeatRight Ltd, a Gas Safe registered heating contractor, to visit on Sunday 11 October between 8am and 12pm. Please keep the morning free and let them in. Their engineer may need to check the boiler and the heating system.

If you smell gas, leave the property, do not use switches or flames, and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999. If you feel unwell or unsafe at any point, call 999.

If the visit time changes, we will email you. Please reply to this email if you have any questions.

Kind regards,
Property management team
